claims.text: MaxKernel is a multi-agent system that implements three distinct paradigms for TPU kernel development: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), Autonomous (Auto), and Graph-Based Autonomous Search.
claims.poster_quote: In this work, we present MaxKernel, a multi-agent system that implements three distinct paradigms for TPU kernel development: (1) a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) agent for collaborative, step-by-step design; (2) an Autonomous (Auto) agent that executes a fully automated, metric/trace-driven optimization loop; and (3) a Graph-Based Autonomous Search that scales the Auto agent for global exploration of the design space.

claims.paper_evidence: In this work, we present MaxKernel, a multi-agent system that implements three distinct paradigms for TPU kernel development: (1) a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) agent for collaborative, step-by-step design; (2) an Autonomous (Auto) agent that executes a fully automated, metric/trace-driven optimization loop; and (3) a Graph-Based Autonomous Search that scales the Auto agent for global exploration of the design space.
claims.reason: This statement is directly stated in the abstract (Page 1, Paragraph 1).

claims.poster_quote: This abstraction enables experimentation with search heuristics, graceful recovery from unexpected halts via persistent graph state, and mitigation of LLM context overflow by isolating each node expansion into a separate agent session.

claims.reason: This statement is directly stated in Section 2.5 (Page 5, Paragraph 1).

claims.reason: This statement is directly stated in Section 3.1 (Page 7, Paragraph 1).

claims.text: The harness integrates XProf to capture precise on-device execution times, filtering host-side JAX dispatch and compilation overheads.
claims.poster_quote: The harness integrates XProf to capture precise on-device execution times, filtering host-side JAX dispatch and compilation overheads.

claims.reason: This statement is directly stated in Section 3.1 (Page 7, Paragraph 1).

claims.text: Methods compared include Best-of-N (Zero-Shot) with N=100, MaxKernel Auto (single trajectory, 5 iterations, median over 5 runs), MaxKernel Parallel (5 concurrent Auto trajectories, best correct kernel), and MaxKernel Beam (beam width 3, max depth 3, 2 branches per node, 2 iterations per node).
claims.poster_quote: Methods compared: Best-of-N (Zero-Shot) with N=100; MaxKernel Auto (single trajectory, 5 iterations, median over 5 runs); MaxKernel Parallel (5 concurrent Auto trajectories, best correct kernel); MaxKernel Beam (beam width 3, max depth 3, 2 branches per node, 2 iterations per node).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We compare the following four generation methods: • Best-of- 𝑁 (Zero-Shot): Independent zero-shot completions conditioned on the JAX reference. The fastest correct sample out of 𝑁 is selected (in our experiments, we set 𝑁 = 100). • MaxKernel Auto: A single-trajectory iterative refinement agent restricted to 5 iterations. To account for generation variance, we execute 5 independent runs per workload and report the median performance with its upper and lower bounds. • MaxKernel Parallel: Executed via 5 concurrent MaxKernel Auto trajectories (5 iterations each). Instead of the median, it selects the single fastest correct kernel across all runs, highlighting the upper bound of unguided parallel scaling. • MaxKernel Beam: A structured, top-𝑘 guided graph search configured with a beam width of 3, a maximum depth of 3, and 2 expansion branches per node. To limit computational cost, the inner evaluation loop is strictly capped at 2 iterations per node.
claims.reason: This statement is directly stated in Section 3.1 (Page 7, Paragraph 1).

claims.poster_quote: Parallel Search is unconstrained exploration: it concurrently executes multiple independent trajectories from a baseline; since paths do not compete, each worker gets a larger iteration budget, granting a deep horizon to debug and mature complex code changes.

claims.paper_evidence: Parallel Search acts as an unconstrained exploration mechanism; it concurrently executes multiple independent optimization trajectories from a given baseline.
claims.reason: This statement is directly stated in Section 2.5 (Page 6, Paragraph 1).

claims.text: Beam Search is highly competitive, maintaining a restricted frontier of the top-k most promising kernels.

claims.text: MaxKernel resolved critical crash and deadlock issues in Ragged Paged Attention v3 prefill mode by automatically implementing protective ALU clamp instructions for left-padded inputs.
claims.poster_quote: Beyond performance, MaxKernel aided debugging and robustness: it resolved critical crash and deadlock issues in Ragged Paged Attention v3 prefill mode by automatically implementing protective ALU clamp instructions for left-padded inputs, preventing negative slice sizes and ensuring DMA prefetches execute cleanly—restoring crash-free execution with negligible overhead.
